title: `ascii`: the first character's code point, also past ASCII
verdict: `ascii` of a non-ASCII first character is its code point; the reference raises (`non_ascii_text: ERROR`, D43)
description: `ascii(s)` is the Unicode code point of the first character of `s`, whether or not it is ASCII: `ascii('Ω')` and `ascii('ΩΩ')` are 937, `ascii('Ä')` is 196, `ascii('ABC')` is 65.
reference: `ascii` of text with a character past ASCII raises `Issue.nonAscii` under `non_ascii_text: ERROR` (D43), where the engines can differ; on ASCII text it is the code point, as DuckDB's. The written SQL raises on the same predicate.

evidence.note: ASCII('Ω') → 937, ASCII('ΩΩ') → 937, ASCII('Ä') → 196; the file is the same at v2.0.0

provenance.notes: Replayed at 2.0.1 by `sverify_dev.slt`: DuckDB's control gives the expected values; Lean raises nonAscii and the written plan's guard raises, so the ledger records the three queries as disagree (both), explained by this fact.
